Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:

  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Test has fill/interior color 9, regular separator color 2; horizontal separator rows 0, 8, 16 and vertical separator columns 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20, 23 (0-indexed). Sample crossings at these lines. ## Rule
The input is an enlarged lattice: a regular set of horizontal and vertical separator lines surrounds large uniform interior areas. Identify the repeated line coordinates and the uniform interior/fill color. At every pair of adjacent horizontal lines and pair of adjacent vertical lines, form a candidate output cell from the four separator-crossing corner values. If all four corner values are the same non-fill marker color, put that color in the candidate cell; otherwise leave the candidate as the interior/fill color. Finally, trim the candidate output to the tight bounding box of cells that differ from the fill color. Preserve a 1x1 output when that is the remaining box.

In these examples the line crossings can be read where the periodic horizontal and vertical separator bands intersect. The broad regions between them are uniform fill. Do not output the input separator grid itself, and do not guess output dimensions by retaining blank candidate rows/columns: crop the all-fill margins.

Test input 17x23 has fill color 3; separators at rows 2 and 15, and columns 4, 10, 16, 22. There is one candidate output row and three candidate columns.
